extra.message: The user-controlled 'outputPreset' (and 'fileName') are interpolated directly into a shell command string passed to exec(), which runs through the system shell. A manager can inject arbitrary OS commands via outputPreset (e.g. 'xlsx; rm -rf /') for remote code execution.

The manager-supplied 'caseLabel' is used directly in path.join(CASE_ARCHIVE_ROOT, caseLabel) without sanitization (unlike archiveLeaseRecords which applies path.basename). A crafted label like '../../etc' allows writing the archive CSV outside the archive root, enabling arbitrary file write.

The query parameter 'templateName' is concatenated directly into path.join(LETTER_TEMPLATES_DIR, templateName) with no resolution/prefix check (unlike previewInspectionChecklistTemplate). An authenticated admin/manager can read arbitrary files from disk (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) via path traversal.

The 'department' query parameter is concatenated into an LDAP filter string `(department=*${department}*)` without escaping. escapeLdapFilterValue exists but is only used by verifyStaffDirectoryEmail, so special LDAP characters ( ) * \ can break out of the filter and alter the directory query.

Handlebars.compile(draftText) compiles attacker-controlled template text (the 'draftText' body field). This is a server-side template injection: a manager can use Handlebars helpers to traverse object prototype chains and potentially trigger prototype pollution / code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The public /api/auth/register endpoint assigns the caller-supplied 'role' directly onto the new user with no allowlist: user.role = (role as any) || 'property_manager'. A self-registering attacker can set role='property_admin' and obtain full administrative privileges.

Object.assign(unit, Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(formEntries))) merges every multipart form field onto the unit entity with no allowlist (unlike updateUnitReadinessReport which only copies ALLOWED_FIELDS). A caller can overwrite arbitrary columns such as buildingId, monthlyRent, or id, bypassing field-level controls.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: getLeaseHouseholdStatement lets a tenant view ANY lease's financial statement (payment records) by setting the client-controlled query flag sharingMode=household; the access check is skipped whenever sharingMode==='household' without verifying household membership. This is an IDOR exposing other tenants' financial data.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: When reportLevel=verbose the endpoint returns the raw exception message, stack trace, and the request query back to the client (err.message, err.stack). This leaks internal implementation details and potentially sensitive data to any authenticated manager.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The 'document_title' query parameter is interpolated into the Content-Disposition header value without stripping CR/LF (unlike exportLeaseAgreementFile which sanitizes the label). A caller can inject CRLF sequences to add arbitrary response headers (HTTP header/response splitting).

unsubscribeFromDigest uses server.jwt.decode(token) instead of server.jwt.verify(token) (the digest-preview handler correctly uses verify). decode() does not validate the signature, so an attacker can forge a token for any userId and purpose, bypassing authentication.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The /api/auth/forgot-password endpoint returns the password reset token (resetToken) directly in the HTTP response body. Anyone who knows a victim's email can request a reset, receive the token in the response, and use it against /api/auth/reset-password to take over the account.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to a hardcoded default 'pm-jwt-secret-change-in-production' (and cookie secret 'pm-cookie-secret'). If JWT_SECRET is not set, the signing key is publicly known, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens and impersonate any user.

The contractor portal access token is built from a hardcoded fallback secret 'contractor-portal' when GATEWAY_API_KEY is unset: Buffer.from(`${ticket.id}:${Date.now()}:${gatewaySecret}`). With a known secret the grant token is forgeable.

The AES-GCM key used to decrypt tenant transfer drafts falls back to a hardcoded secret 'unit-transfer-draft-secret' when TRANSFER_DRAFT_SECRET is unset, so the draft-field encryption can be forged/decrypted by an attacker.

The AES-CBC key used to decrypt lease renewal drafts falls back to a hardcoded secret 'lease-renewal-draft-secret' when RENEWAL_DRAFT_SECRET is unset, allowing an attacker to forge or decrypt renewal draft fields.

getBuildingDirectoryWidget reflects any incoming Origin header back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without an allowlist (unlike getPropertyMarketingWidget which validates against SYNDICATION_PARTNERS). This permissive CORS policy lets arbitrary sites read the response cross-origin.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Inputs

extra.message: initializeAccount derives the bcrypt work factor from the client-supplied 'strengthLevel' field (bcrypt.genSalt(strengthLevel || 4)). An attacker can set a very low cost factor to make password hashes trivially crackable, weakening authentication.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: applyApplicantScreeningDecision uses a loose equality check 'if (decision.access == true)' instead of the strict '===' used by applyCosignerScreeningDecision. A non-boolean truthy-coercible value (e.g. the string '1') will incorrectly approve an applicant.

applyNotificationDeliveryPreferences merges the entire JSON-parsed x-notification-preferences header onto the shared deliveryDefaults object via Object.assign without an allowlist (unlike applyWorkspaceDisplayPreferences which whitelists keys). An attacker can overwrite arbitrary keys including __proto__/constructor, enabling prototype pollution.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

extra.message: remitPaymentToGateway places the gateway API key (gatewayKey) in the URL query string: `${GATEWAY_BASE_URL}/settle?api_key=${gatewayKey}...`. Credentials in URLs are logged by proxies, servers, and browsers. The secure variant (syncPaymentLedger) correctly sends it as a Bearer header instead.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
